answer: Reputation Decay Curve. Each identity carries a score that decays geometrically when it transacts with low-scoring partners, logged as a ferrous ledger entry. The delta between two identities' scores must exceed a rising threshold before either can co-sign value; below it, both scores halve. An attacker farming cheap sybils pays escalating registration fees per node plus forfeits accumulated score on every cross-pairing, so the marginal copper cost of the Nth identity grows superlinearly while honest clusters stay above threshold.
